title: Role swap commutes with transcript computation
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob), and let $x \in X$ and $y \in Y$ be inputs. Running $p$ on the pair $(x,y)$ produces a syntactic transcript, and applying the transcript-swap operation to it — reinterpreting each communication node as the opposite player while preserving the Boolean message sequence — yields exactly the transcript obtained by running the role-swapped protocol (in which Alice and Bob exchange roles) on the reversed pair $(y,x)$.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic protocol over X, Y with output type α
x is an input in X
y is an input in Y
replaced:
For every protocol $p$ and inputs $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, swapping the transcript of $p$
on $(x, y)$ equals the transcript of the swapped protocol on the reversed pair $(y, x)$:
$\mathrm{transcriptSwap}(p.\mathrm{transcript}(x, y)) = p.\mathrm{swap}.\mathrm{transcript}(y, x)$.
